newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says Rifkind's Mideast forum premature.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says Rifkind's Mideast forum premature.

text.p: Egypt applauded on Tuesday British Foreign Minister Malcom Rifkind for his Middle East peace initiatives but said his proposal to set up a regional body to help reduce conflicts was premature.

Rifkind, on a regional tour designed to give new impetus to the peace process, told reporters in the United Arab Emirates on Monday that the Middle East would benefit from a forum that includes all the countries in the region and that would "provide a framework for dialogue and collaboration."
He suggested it be called the Organisation for Cooperation in the Middle East (OCME) and function like the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
"Egypt fully agrees with every word Rifkind has said on the importance of the peace process and its components," Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told reporters.

"We cannot begrudge Mr. Rifkind his futuristic outlook and Europe's concern for the region but there's a time for everything. At this point, it (the OCME) would be putting the cart before the horse...and the horse is peace," Moussa added.
Israel has yet to finalise peace accords with Syria, Lebanon and the Palestinians.
Arabs have said they do not see soon progress unless Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu abandons some policies like building Jewish settlements on occupied Palestinian land.
Rifkind did not mention Israel but said he hoped Turkey, Iran and Iraq could join the organisation.
